headline: 1 dead, 40 injured as clash over char land ownership erupts in Cumilla
summary: A violent confrontation between residents of two villages over disputed land on the Titas-Meghna border left one woman dead and dozens injured.
details: A 35-year-old woman, Kohinur Begum, was killed and at least 40 people were injured during a violent clash between residents of two villages in Cumilla on Sunday afternoon.
The conflict broke out between residents of Char Bhatera village in Titas upazila and those from Alipur and Char Binatpur villages in Meghna upazila over the ownership of a disputed char land.
According to police, the tension escalated after two residents of Char Bhatera were allegedly assaulted and detained at the Meghna Sub-Registrar’s Office earlier in the day.
The confrontation turned into a two-hour battle involving spears, resulting in 15 injuries from Titas and 25 from Meghna.
The wounded were admitted to Titas and Meghna Upazila Health Complexes, with three critically injured victims referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Additional police personnel have been deployed to both areas to maintain law and order, and the situation is reported to be under control since Sunday evening.
A similar clash over the ownership of the same char land along the Titas-Meghna border had previously occurred on June 15, leading to widespread vandalism.

headline_marked: 60 injured, [[woman killed in land dispute clash]] in Cumilla
headline: 60 injured, woman killed in land dispute clash in Cumilla
summary: A violent conflict over the possession of newly emerged land in the Kanthalia River occurred between residents of five villages, leaving one woman dead and dozens injured.
details: A 35-year-old woman, Kohinur Akhtar, was killed after being hit by a spear (teta) during a clash over the possession of newly emerged land in the Kanthalia River, Cumilla.

The conflict broke out on Sunday afternoon between residents of Char Binodpur village in Meghna upazila and residents of Nandirchar, Dudhgata, Notun Batera, and Puratan Batera villages in Titas upazila.
At least 60 people were injured in the violence, with many suffering from spear wounds. Some of the most critically injured were sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for specialized treatment.

The dispute is centered on a newly emerged landmass (char) in the Kanthalia River. Residents of Char Binodpur claim ownership based on 20 years of tax payments, while others attempted to register the land.
Villagers from Char Binodpur allege that an attack was launched on them, resulting in the destruction of over 50 residential houses. Their residents now report living in fear and insecurity.

Meghna Police Station OC Mohidul Islam confirmed the death of Kohinur Akhtar and sent her body to Cumilla Medical College Hospital for autopsy. Police have brought the situation under control and are investigating the case.
